title: Maximum Depth of a Binary Tree
contract: Build a binary tree from a level-order array using null for absent nodes. Return the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.
brute: Tree root=tree(input);if(root==null)return 0;List<List<Tree>> paths=new ArrayList<>();Deque<List<Tree>> pending=new ArrayDeque<>();pending.push(new ArrayList<>(List.of(root)));while(!pending.isEmpty()){List<Tree> path=pending.pop();Tree last=path.get(path.size()-1);paths.add(path);for(Tree child:new Tree[]{last.left,last.right})if(child!=null){List<Tree> next=new ArrayList<>(path);next.add(child);pending.push(next);}emit("Copy each root-to-node path","path length",path.size());}return paths.stream().mapToInt(List::size).max().orElse(0);
optimal: Tree root=tree(input);if(root==null)return 0;Deque<Tree> q=new ArrayDeque<>();q.add(root);int depth=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){int size=q.size();for(int i=0;i<size;i++){Tree node=q.remove();if(node.left!=null)q.add(node.left);if(node.right!=null)q.add(node.right);}depth++;emit("Finish exactly one level","depth",depth,"next level size",q.size());}return depth;
reasoning: Store complete root-to-node paths and take the longest; copying paths wastes work on skewed trees.
Level-order traversal processes a fixed queue size before incrementing depth.
The queue contains only the frontier. A recursive alternative returns 1 + max(leftHeight,rightHeight) with O(h) call-stack space.
complexity: O(n), O(w) traversal space; w widest level
